sections.text_ja_canonical: 聞くときは、場所の感じ方について、理由を示す言葉に注目してください。

sections.source_en: Each morning, one worker enters the office and looks for an empty desk. Another chooses a quiet corner or a busy place near other teams.
Some companies are bringing back personal desks. Others still use shared desks. Why does the same office feel safe to one person and free to another?

sections.text_ja_canonical: 同じ職場でも、安心できる場所や働きやすい場所は人によって違います。ここからは、その違いをそれぞれの立場から語る声を順番に聞いていきましょう。

sections.source_en: One Voice: A desk that helps me start.

Every morning, I look for an empty desk. Someone may have used it yesterday, and someone else may use it tomorrow. I cannot keep papers in a drawer. I sometimes worry about using a desk or keyboard after someone else. I spend time finding a place before work starts. I miss having the same desk, drawer, and view. They helped me start without looking around and gave me a quiet feeling that I belonged there. Now the office can feel like a place I only borrow. I want my work and things to have a place, even when I cannot choose the desk rules.

Some mornings, I choose a quiet corner because I need to think. On other days, I sit where talking is easy. A different desk can put me near people from another department. It can also give me space when a work relationship feels uncomfortable. Sometimes I simply need room. Working from home gave me a place of my own, so I do not need one fixed place at the office. I like changing my surroundings. I choose a place that fits my mood and task. I also choose who is near me—or whether I want anyone near me.

sections.text_ja_canonical: 二つの声では、同じ状況でも、感じ方が違っていました。ここでは、どちらが正しいかを決めるのではなく、なぜ同じ状況が人によって違って感じられるのかを考えます。その理由を、これから見ていきましょう。

sections.source_en: The disagreement is not really about moving. It is about the source of stability. One worker finds stability in a desk that stays in one place. Papers and a familiar start help this person. The other finds stability in the power to change who is nearby. The kind of space this person needs can also change each day. A shared-desk system can even lead people to use the same desk often. So a rule may look flexible on paper but feel difficult to one person. The same system may feel useful to another.

sections.text_ja_canonical: ここで大切なのは、どちらが正しいかを決めることではありません。同じ仕組みが違って感じられるのは、安定を感じる条件が人によって違うからです。では、何がこの状況を成り立たせているのでしょうか。

sections.source_en: The real question is not fixed desks or shared desks. It is what makes a place work. One person needs a steady point. It removes the need to search every day. Another needs enough control to change the people nearby and the work space. The seat is only the visible part of a deeper question: What makes a worker feel, “This is my place at work”?
